title: Comparisons and briefings: code aligns, AI explains
outcome: Build exact comparison and grouping inputs before asking for a useful narrative.
cue: Code lines up the evidence. AI can make it easier to read.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Build exact comparison and grouping inputs before asking for a useful narrative.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: Dropping inaccessible selected records silently can produce a misleading comparison. A narrative may also relabel a correct number to the wrong category.

trace.title: Permitted bounded selection
trace.detail:
Comparing several records is a different task from looking up one. Code must verify access to every selected record, align the same fields, preserve missing values, and derive exact differences. The model can explain which supplied differences appear relevant, but it cannot create new facts or decide authorization.

For a work-queue briefing, compute groups and counts in code under the same active filter/scope. A narrative can suggest an order of attention, but its counts and labels must match the supplied aggregates. Keep “not available” distinct from zero and “same” distinct from “not compared.”

Bound selection size and context. The user should be able to inspect the underlying comparison or group table without the generated text. That deterministic view is useful when AI is unavailable or unhelpful.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Selection/filter → access check for all records → aligned facts or exact groups → bounded context → generated draft → field/number checks → inspectable deterministic table. Test a mixed-authority selection and an empty result.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Dropping inaccessible selected records silently can produce a misleading comparison. A narrative may also relabel a correct number to the wrong category.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Build exact comparison and grouping inputs before asking for a useful narrative. Give a concrete example, one failure, and the check that catches it.
